Restated at replacement capex: LLY spent $23,144mm on plant over 2018 to 2025 against $7,255mm of plant depreciation, 5.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 27.30% to 20.25%. Restated without working capital build: over 2018 to 2025 LLY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $15,658mm, inventories up $10,223mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $18,257mm, a working capital build of $7,624mm, 2.83% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 20.25% to 16.87%.

column11: lookup.py demand Trodelvy: Part B 2024, $272,318,588 over 3,300 beneficiaries = $82,521 per beneficiary. The same anchor is on the AZD5335 seed (lookup.py seed AZD5335).
column12: JUDGEMENT. The closest marketed comparator is Elahere (mirvetuximab), the Part A comparator arm, but the book has no CMS demand row for it (lookup.py demand %lahere% / %oravtan% return nothing), and no published annual list price was found. Trodelvy is used for two reasons: it is a topo-I ADC in a solid tumour, and it keeps this asset on the same price as AZD5335, the book's other FRa ADC in this disease. Case against: Elahere's launch WAC was $6,220 a vial, about $18,660 to $24,800 per 21-day cycle (Managed Healthcare Executive, https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/fda-grants-accelerated-approval-of-novel-ovarian-cancer-therapy). Over a real-world median of 8 cycles that is about $174k gross per course, roughly twice this anchor. At this price and gross-to-net, Elahere's $607mm of US 2025 revenue would imply about 14,700 patient-years, which is not plausible. The anchor is therefore probably low for this class.

column11: Value in Health HSD30 / ISPOR 2024 poster 139151, 'Incidence of Platinum-Resistant, Stage III/IV Ovarian Cancer Patients in the US' (https://www.valueinhealthjournal.com/article/S1098-3015(24)01368-8/fulltext). In 2023, 6,224, 4,329 and 2,901 patients were treated in lines 2, 3 and 4, with 14.7%, 40.5% and 59.1% platinum-resistant. That is 915 + 1,753 + 1,714 = 4,382 PROC patients treated in lines 2 to 4. 4,382 / 21,010 = 0.209.
column12: JUDGEMENT on the arithmetic. This matches Part A's population: PROC after 3 or fewer prior lines, at all FRa levels, so no FRa cut is applied. It assumes the eventual label is not FRa-restricted. Caveats: the counts are line-treatment events, so one patient can appear in both line 3 and line 4. The ISPOR base is 14,768 stage III/IV cases (IARC), not the book's 21,010. One search summary gave the line-3 count as 2,901, so the second reader should confirm the per-line figures. The pool looks low against Elahere revenue (see penetration). The platinum-sensitive Parts B and C are not modelled.
